---
title: "Notation"
---

This site uses the book's notation. Symbols are added here as chapters are written.

| Symbol | Meaning | First used |
|---|---|---|
| $P(x)$ | Probability mass function (discrete): the probability that $X = x$ | Ch 2 |
| $p(x)$ | Probability density function (continuous); probabilities are areas under it | Ch 2 |
| $\operatorname{cdf}(x)$ | Cumulative distribution function, $P(X \le x)$ | Ch 2 |
| $\mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu, \sigma^2)$ | Gaussian with mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$; $\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{x} \mid \boldsymbol\mu, \boldsymbol\Sigma)$ is the multivariate version | Ch 2 |
| $\mathcal{U}(x \mid a, b)$ | Uniform distribution on $[a, b]$ | Ch 2 |
| $\rho_i$ | Weight of component $i$ in a mixture | Ch 2 |
| $x^0$, $x^1$ | The two values of a binary variable: no, yes | Ch 2 |
| $P(x \mid y)$ | Conditional probability of $x$ given $y$ | Ch 2 |
| $\theta_1$, $\theta_2$ | Threshold and softness of a sigmoid conditional | Ch 2 |
| $x_{1:n}$ | The values $x_1, \ldots, x_n$ | Ch 2 |
| $\mathrm{pa}(x_i)$ | Values of the parents of $X_i$ in a Bayesian network | Ch 2 |
| $(X \perp Y \mid Z)$ | $X$ and $Y$ are conditionally independent given $Z$ | Ch 2 |
| $q$, $e$, $h$ | Query, evidence, and hidden variables in an inference problem | Ch 3 |
| $\theta$ | Model parameters, such as CPT entries | Ch 4 |
| $\ell(\theta)$ | Log-likelihood of the data under parameters $\theta$ | Ch 4 |
| $m_{ijk}$ | Count of records with variable $i$ at value $k$ and its parents at combination $j$ | Ch 4 |
| $\hat\theta$ | An estimate of $\theta$ | Ch 4 |
| $\mathrm{Beta}(\theta \mid \alpha, \beta)$ | Beta distribution over a probability $\theta$; $\alpha$, $\beta$ act as pseudocounts | Ch 4 |
| $\mathrm{Dir}(\theta_{1:n} \mid \alpha_{1:n})$ | Dirichlet distribution over $n$ probabilities that sum to 1 | Ch 4 |
| $\phi$, $h$ | Kernel and bandwidth in kernel density estimation | Ch 4 |
| $G$, $D$ | A graph (network structure) and a dataset | Ch 5 |
| $\ln P(G \mid D)$ | Bayesian score of graph $G$ on data $D$ | Ch 5 |
| $\Gamma(x)$ | Gamma function; $\Gamma(n) = (n-1)!$ for whole numbers | Ch 5 |
| $\alpha_{ijk}$, $\alpha_{ij0}$, $m_{ij0}$ | Pseudocount for a cell, and the row totals of pseudocounts and counts | Ch 5 |
| $q_i$, $r_i$ | Number of parent combinations and number of values of variable $i$ | Ch 5 |
| $\kappa$ | Equivalent sample size of a BDeu prior | Ch 5 |
| $\mathrm{pa}_G(x_i)$ | Parents of $x_i$ in graph $G$ | Ch 5 |
| $\phi$ | A factor: a table over some variables (a CPT, or any partial product) | Ch 3 |
| $P(c \mid o_{1:n})$ | Naive Bayes posterior of class $c$ given observations $o_1, \ldots, o_n$ | Ch 3 |
| $w$ | Likelihood weight of a sample | Ch 3 |
| $x_{-i}$ | All variables except $x_i$ | Ch 3 |
| $\boldsymbol{\mu}_{a \mid b}$, $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{a \mid b}$ | Mean and covariance of Gaussian block $\mathbf{a}$ given block $\mathbf{b}$ | Ch 3 |
| $A \succ B$, $A \sim B$, $A \succeq B$ | $A$ preferred to $B$; indifferent; at least as good | Ch 6 |
| $[S_1 : p_1; \ldots; S_n : p_n]$ | Lottery: outcome $S_i$ with probability $p_i$ | Ch 6 |
| $U(S)$ | Utility of outcome $S$ | Ch 6 |
| $S_\top$, $S_\bot$ | Best and worst outcomes, used to scale utility to $[0, 1]$ | Ch 6 |
| $x_{\text{ce}}$ | Certainty equivalent: the sure amount worth the same as a gamble | Ch 6 |
| $\lambda$ | Risk-aversion parameter of exponential utility $1 - e^{-\lambda x}$ | Ch 6 |
| $EU(a \mid o)$, $EU^*(o)$ | Expected utility of action $a$ given observation $o$; its maximum over actions | Ch 6 |
| $\mathrm{VOI}(O' \mid o)$ | Value of information of observing $O'$, given $o$ | Ch 6 |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | State space | Ch 7 |
| $\mathcal{A}$ | Action space | Ch 7 |
| $T(s' \mid s, a)$ | Transition model: probability of reaching $s'$ from $s$ after action $a$ | Ch 7 |
| $R(s, a)$ | Expected reward for taking action $a$ in state $s$ | Ch 7 |
| $\gamma$ | Discount factor, $0 \le \gamma \le 1$ | Ch 7 |
| $\pi$ | Policy: maps states to actions | Ch 7 |
| $U^\pi(s)$ | Value (utility) of state $s$ under policy $\pi$ | Ch 7 |
| $U^*(s)$ | Optimal value of state $s$ | Ch 7 |
| $U_k$ | Value estimate after $k$ sweeps of value iteration | Ch 7 |
| $Q(s, a)$ | Action value: reward for $a$ in $s$ plus the discounted value $U$ of where you land | Ch 7 |
| $A(s, a)$ | Advantage: $Q(s, a) - U(s)$ | Ch 7 |
| $\mathbf{T}^\pi$, $\mathbf{R}^\pi$ | Transition matrix and reward vector with the policy's action fixed in each state | Ch 7 |
| $\lVert U \rVert_\infty$ | Largest absolute entry, $\max_s \lvert U(s) \rvert$ | Ch 7 |
| $\delta$, $\epsilon$ | Bellman-residual threshold and target accuracy in value iteration | Ch 7 |
| $U_\theta(s)$, $Q_\theta(s, a)$ | Parametric (approximate) value and action value functions with parameters $\theta$ | Ch 8 |
| $S = s_{1:m}$ | Sample states where approximate value iteration does backups | Ch 8 |
| $\beta(s)$ | Basis functions (features), or local weights, so that $U_\theta(s) = \theta^\top \beta(s)$ | Ch 8 |
| $d(s, s')$, $k(s, s')$ | Distance between states, and a kernel (larger for closer states) | Ch 8 |
| $\sigma$ | Width of a Gaussian kernel | Ch 8 |
| $X$, $X^+$ | Feature matrix (row $i$ is $\beta(s_i)^\top$) and its pseudoinverse | Ch 8 |
| $d$ | Search depth (planning horizon) of an online planner | Ch 9 |
| $U_d(s)$ | Value of $s$ from a depth-$d$ search | Ch 9 |
| $\underline{U}(s)$, $\overline{Q}(s, a)$, $\overline{U}(s)$ | Lower bound on values; upper bounds on action values and values (admissible heuristic) | Ch 9 |
| $m$ | Number of samples (sparse sampling) or simulations (MCTS, heuristic search) | Ch 9 |
| $N(s, a)$, $N(s)$ | Visit counts in Monte Carlo tree search | Ch 9 |
| $c$ | Exploration constant in UCB1 | Ch 9 |
| $\delta$ | Residual threshold for a state to count as solved | Ch 9 |
| $a_{1:d}$ | An open-loop sequence of actions | Ch 9 |
| $\pi_\theta$, $U(\theta)$ | A policy with parameters $\theta$, and its expected return | Ch 10 |
| $\tau$, $R(\tau)$, $p_\pi(\tau)$ | A trajectory, its discounted return, and its probability under $\pi$ | Ch 10 |
| $b(s)$ | Initial state distribution (for policy search) | Ch 10 |
| $\alpha$, $c$, $\epsilon$ | Step size, its reduction factor, and the stopping step size (Hooke–Jeeves) | Ch 10 |
| $m_{\text{elite}}$ | Number of elite samples kept each iteration | Ch 10 |
| $p(\theta \mid \psi)$ | Search distribution over policy parameters, with parameters $\psi$ | Ch 10 |
| $w^{(i)}$ | Rank-shaped weight of the $i$-th best sample | Ch 10 |
| $\nabla U(\theta)$ | Policy gradient: how the expected return changes with each parameter | Ch 11 |
| $\delta$, $e_i$ | Finite-difference step, and the unit vector along parameter $i$ | Ch 11 |
| $\Delta\Theta$, $\Delta U$ | Matrix of parameter perturbations (one per row) and the resulting changes in $U$ | Ch 11 |
| $\pi_\theta(a \mid s)$ | Probability (or density) that the policy takes action $a$ in state $s$ | Ch 11 |
| $\nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a \mid s)$ | Score of an action: the direction that makes it more likely | Ch 11 |
| $r_{\text{to-go}}^{(k)}$ | Reward-to-go: discounted reward from step $k$ on | Ch 11 |
| $r_{\text{base}}(s)$ | Baseline subtracted from the reward-to-go | Ch 11 |
| $A(s, a)$ | Advantage: $Q(s, a) - U(s)$ | Ch 11 |
| $F_\theta$ | Fisher information matrix of the policy's trajectory distribution | Ch 12 |
| $D_{\text{KL}}(p \,\Vert\, q)$ | Kullback–Leibler divergence from $p$ to $q$ | Ch 12 |
| $\epsilon$ | Trust-region size (KL or step budget); PPO's clipping range | Ch 12 |
| $f(\theta, \theta')$, $g(\theta, \theta')$ | TRPO's surrogate objective and surrogate KL constraint | Ch 12 |
| $b_{\gamma,\theta}(s)$ | Discounted state-visitation distribution of $\pi_\theta$ | Ch 12 |
| $w = \pi_{\theta'}(a \mid s) / \pi_\theta(a \mid s)$ | Probability ratio (importance weight) | Ch 12 |
| $U_\phi(s)$, $Q_\phi(s, a)$ | The critic: a value function with parameters $\phi$ | Ch 13 |
| $\delta_k$ | Temporal difference residual $r_k + \gamma U(s_{k+1}) - U(s_k)$ | Ch 13 |
| $\hat A^{(k)}$, $\hat A^{\text{GAE}}$ | $k$-step and generalized advantage estimates | Ch 13 |
| $\lambda$ | GAE weight between TD residuals ($\lambda = 0$) and full returns ($\lambda = 1$) | Ch 13 |
| $\nabla_\theta \pi_\theta(s)$ | Jacobian of a deterministic policy (one column per action component) | Ch 13 |
| $\pi_{\text{MCTS}}$, $U_{\text{MCTS}}$, $\eta$ | Tree search's visit-count policy (sharpened by $\eta$) and value | Ch 13 |
| $f(\pi)$ | A performance metric of policy $\pi$: the expected trajectory metric | Ch 14 |
| $f_{\text{traj}}$, $f_{\text{step}}$, $f_{\text{state}}$ | Metric of a trajectory, of one step, and its expected total from a state | Ch 14 |
| $b(s_1)$ | Start (initial state) distribution; in Ch 19 on, $b$ is a belief | Ch 14 |
| $\text{SE} = \hat\sigma/\sqrt n$ | Standard error of a sample mean; divided by $\hat\mu$, the relative standard error | Ch 14 |
| $P'(\tau)$, $P^*(\tau)$ | Proposal distribution for importance sampling; the optimal (zero-variance) proposal | Ch 14 |
| $w = P(\tau)/P'(\tau)$ | Importance weight of a trajectory sampled from the proposal | Ch 14 |
| $T_i$, $R_i$ | The $i$-th of several candidate models in robust dynamic programming | Ch 14 |
| $R'$, $\lambda$ | Adversarial reward, and its weight on the log-likelihood of the adversary's choices | Ch 14 |
| $\theta_a$, $\theta^*$ | Payoff probability of bandit arm $a$; the best arm's | Ch 15 |
| $w_a$, $\ell_a$ | Wins and losses observed on arm $a$ | Ch 15 |
| $\rho_a$ | Posterior probability that the next pull of arm $a$ wins, $(w_a + 1)/(w_a + \ell_a + 2)$ | Ch 15 |
| $\varepsilon$, $\lambda$, $\alpha$, $c$ | Exploration parameters: ε-greedy rate, softmax precision, quantile level, UCB1 constant | Ch 15 |
| $N(a)$, $N$ | Pulls of arm $a$ (here Beta pseudocounts), and their total | Ch 15 |
| $U^*_r$, $Q^*_r$ | Bayes-optimal bandit values with $r$ pulls remaining | Ch 15 |
| $o$ | An observation | Ch 19 |
| $O(o \mid a, s')$ | Observation model: probability of observing $o$ after taking $a$ and landing in $s'$ | Ch 19 |
| $b(s)$ | Belief: probability that the current state is $s$, given the history | Ch 19 |
| $\mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu, \Sigma)$ | Gaussian density at $x$ with mean $\mu$ and covariance $\Sigma$ | Ch 19 |
| $\mathbf{T}_s$, $\mathbf{T}_a$, $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_s$ | Linear-Gaussian dynamics: state matrix, action matrix, process-noise covariance | Ch 19 |
| $\mathbf{O}_s$, $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_o$ | Linear-Gaussian sensor: observation matrix, sensor-noise covariance | Ch 19 |
| $\boldsymbol{\mu}_b$, $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_b$ | Mean and covariance of a Gaussian belief | Ch 19 |
| $\boldsymbol{\mu}_p$, $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_p$ | Mean and covariance after the predict step | Ch 19 |
| $\mathbf{K}$ | Kalman gain | Ch 19 |
| $s^{(i)}$, $w^{(i)}$ | The $i$-th particle and its weight | Ch 19 |
